# tina4-js

> tina4-js (`tina4js` on npm) is a small reactive frontend framework for the browser, written in TypeScript and built to ES2021, with zero runtime dependencies: signals, `html` tagged templates, Web Components (`Tina4Element`), a client-side router, a fetch API client, WebSocket, SSE/NDJSON streaming, PWA, persistent signals, i18n and a debug overlay. It works standalone or as the frontend of a Tina4 Python, PHP, Ruby or Node.js backend, and suits admin panels, dashboards and CRUD apps rather than large SPA teams.

Quick start. Install the Rust `tina4` CLI (`curl -fsSL https://tina4.com/install.sh | sh`, `brew install tina4stack/tap/tina4`, or `irm https://tina4.com/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows), then:

```bash
tina4 init js my-app   # the path is required; runs npm install (fallback: npx tina4js create my-app)
cd my-app
tina4 serve            # esbuild dev server with live reload on http://localhost:3000
```

Or add it to an existing project with `npm install tina4js`. A route plus reactive state:

```ts
import { signal, html, route, router } from 'tina4js';

const count = signal(0);
route('/', () => html`<button @click=${() => count.value++}>Clicked ${count}</button>`);
route('/users/{id}', ({ id }) => html`<p>User ${id}</p>`);
router.start({ target: '#root', mode: 'history' });
```

Gotchas an agent most needs:

- `${value}` in content position is always escaped text, even an HTML or SVG string. To inject markup, bind the property: `<div .innerHTML=${svg}></div>`. `@click=${fn}` binds an event and `?disabled=${sig}` a boolean attribute.
- `route(pattern, handler)` takes the pattern first; the handler receives the path parameters as an object.
- `route()` and `customElements.define()` register on import. The build runs on esbuild (no Vite), so there is no `import.meta.glob`: keep a barrel such as `src/routes/index.ts` with one import per module, and register the `*` catch-all last.
- `api.get(path, { params, headers })`: the options object carries query parameters and headers, not path parameters. A non-2xx response is thrown, not returned, so wrap `api.*` calls in try/catch.
- `computed()` signals are read-only (writing throws); `effect()` runs immediately and returns a dispose function.
- Reading a signal's `.value` tracks it; use `.peek()` to read without tracking. Re-rendering a block that holds an `<input>` loses focus, so read input values at submit time.
- History mode is the default and gives clean URLs; links and `navigate()` take a bare `/path`, never `#/path`.

## Docs

- [Quick reference](https://tina4.com/js/index.md): one-page cheat sheet of the whole API
- [Getting started](https://tina4.com/js/01-getting-started.md): install, scaffold, project layout, dev server
- [Signals](https://tina4.com/js/02-signals.md): signal, computed, effect, batch
- [Persistent signals](https://tina4.com/js/02-storage.md): signals backed by browser storage
- [HTML templates](https://tina4.com/js/03-html-templates.md): the `html` tag, bindings, reactive blocks, escaping
- [Components](https://tina4.com/js/04-components.md): `Tina4Element` Web Components, props, styles, lifecycle
- [Routing](https://tina4.com/js/05-routing.md): routes, parameters, guards, history and hash modes
- [API client](https://tina4.com/js/06-api.md): configuration, auth tokens, interceptors, error handling
- [WebSocket](https://tina4.com/js/07-websocket.md): managed sockets with reconnect and reactive status
- [SSE and NDJSON streaming](https://tina4.com/js/08-sse-streaming.md): streaming responses into signals
- [Backend integration](https://tina4.com/js/13-backend-integration.md): pairing tina4-js with a Tina4 backend
- [Patterns and pitfalls](https://tina4.com/js/15-patterns-and-pitfalls.md): common patterns and the mistakes to avoid
